problem: Find a Cartesian equation of the plane that passes through the point $P(-2,1,-3)$ and is perpendicular to the vector $n=⟨-2,7,-1⟩.$
worked_solution:
First, we note that the position vector of the point $P$ is $p=⟨-2,1,-3⟩$ and the normal vector of the plane is $n=⟨-2,7,-1⟩.$

Using the dot product we can find an equation of the plane as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}(r-p)\cdot n & =0 \\ r\cdot n & =p\cdot n \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =⟨-2,1,-3⟩\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ \\ r\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =14.\end{aligned}
$$

Now, to obtain the Cartesian equation of the plane, we substitute $r=⟨x,y,z⟩$ into the equation above. Hence,

$$
\begin{aligned}⟨x,y,z⟩\cdot ⟨-2,7,-1⟩ & =14 \\ -2x+7y-z & =14 \\ -2x+7y-z-14 & =0.\end{aligned}
$$
